newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: No accord in talks to end Colombian truckers's strike.
newsitem.headline: No accord in talks to end Colombian truckers's strike.

text.p: Talks aimed at ending a two- day-old strike by Colombia's main truck drivers' union broke off late Monday with no agreement over their demands that might put an end to the crippling work stoppage, union and government officials said.

Javier Suarez, head of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association (ACC), said government and union officials had agreed to resume negotiations at 10 a.m. local time (1500 GMT) Tuesday in a bid to end the labour dispute.

Monday's marathon session of talks, which began at about 3 p.m. (2000 GMT), collapsed shortly after 10:30 p.m. (0330 GMT Tuesday) after the heads of leading economic groups failed to agree on union demands for the setting of minimum cargo rates by the government for highway freight, Suarez told reporters.
